report:
**Conclusion:** Your sister’s claim has a kernel of truth, but it overstates what the evidence supports. CLA may produce a *small* reduction in fat mass in some adults, yet evidence that commercially available CLA supplements reliably or meaningfully reduce **abdominal** fat is weak and inconsistent.

The claim is based partly on a small, short randomized trial: 24 obese middle-aged men with metabolic-syndrome features took 4.2 g/day CLA or placebo for four weeks. The authors found a possible decrease in abdominal fat, but no improvement in overall obesity or other cardiovascular risk factors—and explicitly cautioned that the sample was limited.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11477497/

More importantly, a 2023 systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized trials assessed body mass, BMI, waist circumference, fat mass, body-fat percentage, and fat-free mass in adults. Its broad scope reflects the problem: studies differ substantially in populations, CLA isomer mixtures, doses, comparators, and duration. The available evidence may support modest average body-composition changes, but does not establish a dependable, clinically important loss of belly/visceral fat for an individual.  
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-nutrition/article/effects-of-conjugated-linoleic-acid-supplementation-on-anthropometrics-and-body-composition-indices-in-adults-a-systematic-review-and-doseresponse-metaanalysis/A3F12F07BB3118D4F757D901C6E1E366

Safety also tempers the case: research reports potentially adverse metabolic effects, including increased insulin resistance with some CLA formulations/isomers.  
https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0172912

**Bottom line:** CLA is not a proven abdominal-fat reducer and is unlikely to yield visible or health-meaningful results. It should not replace calorie-appropriate eating, physical activity, sleep, or clinician-guided obesity treatment; someone with diabetes, insulin resistance, liver disease, or pregnancy should discuss it with a clinician before use.
